messages:
sara_support: customer onacct-998 complaining about spike in p99 latency and cross-region egress — most traffic should hit us-west but traces show EU hits, billing jumped. ticket: #45672

lia_support: ugh, saw the same from another customer. their API keys are configured to prefer us-west with failover to us-east. they expect sticky routing.

devon_infra: can you paste the failover config for that org? thinking config parse or priority ordering might be wrong after last UI change.

sara_support: pasted below (redacted org id):
```json
{
  "routes": [
    {"region": "us-east-1", "priority": 0, "weight": 0.2},
    {"region": "us-west-2", "priority": 1, "weight": 0.8, "sticky": true, "ttl_ms": 300000}
  ],
  "mode": "failover"
}
```

devon_infra: aha. that ordering is the problem — UI writes array in display order (top->bottom) but runtime expects highest priority=0 as most preferred. we recently changed sort semantics in platform-ui, so the intended primary (us-west-2) ended up with priority 1.

kevin_reliability: followup: why did sticky routing not keep sessions in us-west? sticky:true + ttl_ms 300000 should.

devon_infra: two things: 1) because priority flipped, requests hit us-east where sticky wasn't set. 2) our sticky cookie logic has a TTL-parse quirk where small decimals in weight/priority cause token to be dropped by the cache layer. there's a related infra-bot alert about cookie-parse errors earlier today.

infra-bot: [alert] cookie-parse-error: 2026-09-03T15:12:09Z - vm-gw-12 - malformed affinity header for client 10.1.44.21 - dropping affinity

lia_support: repro steps from customer: curl to https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate with header `x-api-key: <key>` + `Prefer-Region: us-west-2` and they still see response header `x-rd-served-region: us-east-1` and latency 250ms vs expected 40ms.

devon_infra: trying to repro locally with their key perms — ran:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Prefer-Region: us-west-2" https://api.redwood.example/v1/health
```
Got: `x-rd-routing: fallback->us-east-1`, and server logs show policy eval order: us-east-1 then us-west-2.

kevin_reliability: this explains billing bump — cross-region egress + higher tail latency. what immediate mitigation can support apply for affected orgs?

devon_infra: short-term options: 1) set a temporary override via `/admin/orgs/<org>/routing` to force `primary_region: us-west-2`, 2) remove the weight on the array (forces strict priority interpret), or 3) rollback the UI sorting change (will take longer).

lia_support: can you do option 1 for the two highest-severity customers? I can notify them.

oncall-sre: paging in. I'll patch the admin override endpoint to accept a bulk org list and flip primary_region for the orgs in question. patch will take ~15m.

sara_support: please add a note for customers about any billing adjustments for suspected cross-region egress until next invoice. finance wants us to be proactive.

kevin_reliability: devon, can you also add a runtime guard: if `sticky:true` present on any route, prefer that region regardless of array index until we roll fix? maybe a quick hotfix that checks `sticky` flags before sorting.

devon_infra: on it. I'll push a safe check to staging, smoke test, then prod. trying to avoid full rollback. will include metrics so we can confirm reduction in EU hits.

infra-bot: [deploy] canary: routing-hotfix-v1 -> staging at 1919994605 by devon_infra

devon_infra: smoke results: reduced EU hits for test key from 78% -> 2% on staging. planning prod rollout in 10m.

oncall-sre: rolling to prod now, monitor p99 and `x-rd-served-region` header. if we see any auth regressions, roll back immediately.

infra-bot: [deploy] routing-hotfix-v1 -> prod initiated at 1919994799

lia_support: prod check on real customer keys shows majority of requests now served from us-west-2. lia will send update to customers and create credit request for egress spike.

kevin_reliability: next steps: 1) add e2e tests for UI->runtime priority semantics, 2) fix UI to write priority field semantically (or present clearer label), 3) add lint rule disallowing `priority` gaps/ambiguous order, 4) create a billing alert for cross-region egress anomalies.

sara_support: thanks team. I'll follow up on customer comms and escalate to finance for credits. closing thread after postmortem. :white_check_mark:
